title: Number of Closed Islands
statement: In this grid 0 is LAND and 1 is WATER. An island is a maximal group of land cells connected in 4 directions. It is closed if it is completely surrounded by water, i.e. it touches no edge of the grid. Return the number of closed islands.

hints.1_question: Land that touches the border can never be closed - and neither can any land connected to it. How can you remove all of that first?
hints.2_nudge: Flood-fill from every border land cell, turning it into water. Then count the remaining islands with a normal flood-fill count.
hints.3_big_hint: For each border cell with 0: flood it to 1. Afterwards, for every remaining 0: count += 1 and flood it.

known_bugs.name: counts the islands that touch the border
known_bugs.followup: Is an island that touches the edge closed or not closed?

known_bugs.name: counts every island, closed or not
known_bugs.followup: An island along the edge of the grid is not surrounded by water. Where do you exclude such islands?

known_bugs.name: only removes land connected to the top and left edges
known_bugs.followup: Which edges of the grid does your border check cover? What about the bottom row and right column?
